title: Bank transfer: money appears and disappears
summary: Concurrent transfers between the same accounts create or destroy money and can deadlock.
background: A transfer moves an amount from account A to account B. The invariant every bank must keep is simple: the sum of all balances never changes because of a transfer.

The naive service reads both balances into memory, checks funds, computes the new values and writes them back with SET balance = value_computed. When two transfers touch the same account at the same time, the second write overwrites the first one. The total drifts: money is created or destroyed. This is again a lost update, now across two rows.

Taking row locks fixes the arithmetic but creates a new trap: transfer A to B locks A then B, while transfer B to A locks B then A. Each waits for the other and Postgres kills one with a deadlock error (40P01). The classic fix is to lock both rows in a fixed order (ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE) and then use relative updates: SET balance = balance - amount WHERE balance >= amount.

race.goal: Accounts 1 to 4 start with 1000 each. 20 clients run 5 random transfers each among them. The total must stay 4000 and no balance may be negative.

inner.title: Transfer statement with names
inner.prompt: Show every transfer with the owner name of the source and of the destination account.

left.title: Cards per account, including zero
left.prompt: List every account with how many cards it has. Accounts without cards must show 0.

right.title: Branches without accounts
right.prompt: List every branch with the accounts it holds, keeping branches that hold none.

full.title: KYC reconciliation
full.prompt: Match owners with the KYC vendor file, showing owners never checked and vendor rows for unknown owners.

cross.title: Branch x currency report grid
cross.prompt: Build every branch x currency combination and sum the balance held in each, with 0 when empty.

self.title: Employee and manager
self.prompt: Show every employee next to the name of their manager.

semi.title: Owners with a rich account
semi.prompt: Return owners that have at least one account with more than 5000.

anti.title: Dormant accounts
anti.prompt: Return accounts that never sent nor received a transfer.

lateral.title: Top two transfers per account
lateral.prompt: For every account return its two largest outgoing transfers.
